1. Heard Mr. P.C. Dash, learned counsel for the petitioner and Mr. S.S. Pradhan, learned Addl. Govt.
Advocate for the State.
2.

This is an application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of bail to the petitioner in connection with Talasari Marine P.S. Case No. 43 of 2023 corresponding to C.T. Case No. 278 of 2023 pending in the Court of the learned N.G.N. -cum- J.M.F.C., Bhograi registered for commission of offences punishable under Sections 376(1), 354(c), 506 of IPC read with Sections 66(e) and 67 of I.T. Act.
3.
The petitioner had moved an application for bail before the Court of learned Addl. Sessions Judge, Balasore, Circuit at Jaleswar which was rejected on 04.07.2023.

entities.text: Addl. Sessions Judge, Balasore, Circuit at Jaleswar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 4. The prosecution allegation in brief is that the victim and petitioner were in love with each other.
When the victim learnt that the petitioner has got married, she avoided him and her father arranged her marriage with another person and she got married on 05.08.2019.

After two years of marriage,
she happened to meet the petitioner in her village near Chandaneswar temple.
He threatened her saying that if she did not have relations with him, he will drive her out of her in-laws house by showing her previous nude photos.
He kept physical relations with her under threat and clicked her photograph.
Since the last two months, he uploaded her intimate photograph with him on social media.
When the informant protested, the petitioner threatened to kill her, her husband and her brother and also run over a vehicle over her child.
On the written report of the informant, FIR was registered on 06.06.2023.

Mr. P.C. Dash, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that from the statement of the husband of the victim lady, it is apparent that as the husband found the petitioner and the victim talking to each other for which he switched off the mobile phone of the victim in order to stop them from talking to each other.
This provoked the petitioner to send all the photographs of the victim to her husband as well as the brother and others.

As the victim and the petitioner were in a relationship,
the petitioner was justified to send the photographs and no offence under Section 376 (2) (n) IPC is made out against the petitioner.
The allegations under Section 506 of IPC are false for which he deserves to be released on bail.

6. Mr. Dash, learned counsel placed the statements recorded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C. of the husband of the victim as well as her brother, who have stated that when the husband of the victim came to know that the petitioner and the victim were talking to each other over telephone and maintaining relations, he switched off her mobile to stop them talking, for which the petitioner could not contact the victim anymore.
As a consequence he circulated her nude photographs and has sent them to the husband of the victim as well as the brother and others.

7. Mr. S.S. Pradhan, learned Addl. Govt. Advocate for the State opposes the prayer for bail stating that the petitioner and the victim may have had a relationship but after the victim got married elsewhere the petitioner has compelled her to have relations with him under threat to circulate her photograph and when her husband switched off the mobile and the victim avoided contact with him

,
he has sent her photographs to her husband and other family members.
When she requested him to stop doing so, he threatened her husband and her brother and also threatened to kill her husband and her child.
8. Considering the nature of allegations against the petitioner, I am not inclined to allow the prayer for bail.
The BLAPL is accordingly dismissed.
9. It is open to the petitioner to move for bail afresh after examination of the victim.
10. Urgent certified copy of this order be granted on proper application.
(Savitri Ratho) Judge Sukanta Signed by: SUKANTA KUMAR BEHERA
